fr.elements: Main Building; Secondary Building; Detached Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Internal Drive Aisle; Outdoor Storage Area; Material Storage Area; Dumpster Enclosure; Open Area; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Outdoor Storage; Limited Rear Access; Unpaved Circulation Route
fr.recommendations:
• Mark each building with a visible identifier (e.g., "Building A," "Building B," "Building C") on all sides facing a drive aisle or parking area.

• Post a site map at the main entrance showing the location of all three buildings, the dumpster enclosure, storage areas, and internal drive routes.

• Mark the unpaved circulation route with signage or surface indicators to confirm it is passable for emergency vehicles, or post weight and clearance limits if restrictions apply.

• Keep the internal drive aisle clear of parked vehicles, stored materials, and dumpster overflow to maintain a continuous path between structures.

• Keep outdoor storage and material storage areas organized so a clear path exists around all sides of each building.

• Mark the rear access route at the point where it begins so responders can identify it from the front of the property without driving the full perimeter.

• Keep the area around the dumpster enclosure clear so it does not block vehicle movement along the drive aisle.

• Identify the nearest hydrant or water supply source and post that information at the main site entrance.

wildfire.conditions: Large Paved Area; Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Woody Debris; Open Terrain; Grass Cover; Vegetation Near Building; Multiple Access Routes; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Trees; Open Paved Area
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris visible on the property before it accumulates near buildings or paved areas.
• Trim trees and shrubs growing close to building walls and rooflines.
• Thin the tree cluster to create open spacing between individual trees.
• Cut grass growing across or along the edges of access routes to keep them clear.
• Clear any shrubs or grass that have grown into the limited rear access area to maintain movement around the building.
• Keep scattered shrubs separated from building entrances and exterior walls.
